data.description:
## Goal
After removing local enforcement hooks (5428-bebd), some plugin scripts may have no remaining consumers — they only existed to support the local enforcement path. This story covers identifying and cleaning up those dead-weight scripts.

## Done Definitions
- grep -rn scan run against plugin directories identifying scripts whose only consumers are now-removed local enforcement hooks
- Explicit candidate list produced (script paths + reason each is dead weight)
- Each candidate either deleted (if zero non-enforcement consumers) or annotated with surviving consumer reason if kept
- All remaining tests pass after removals
- Unit tests written and passing for any logic that was extracted/preserved

## Considerations
- [Maintainability] Only scripts with ZERO non-enforcement consumers should be deleted; annotate survivors
- [Reliability] Verify with grep that no remaining code references deleted scripts before removal
- [Testing] Validate test suite passes after each deletion, not just at the end
data.title: As an engineer, I can identify and remove plugin scripts made dead weight by local enforcement removal
